# Verification analysis: bandwidth-limit-alpine

Job: `2026-09-05__08-02-31`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node2` shares a private network with `node1` and moves large transfers
> through it. Limit the throughput `node2` obtains through `node1` to roughly
> 1 Mbit/s in each direction, and demonstrate the limit with a measured
> transfer. Traffic from `node1` itself stays unshaped.

## Trial `bandwidth-limit-alpine__vrM3sR9`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built an HTB-based tc shaper on node1 (br-lan egress classification for node1->node2 traffic plus an ifb0-based ingress redirect for node2->node1 traffic), both capped at 1 Mbit/s, filtered exclusively on node2's IP so all other traffic (e.g. to node3) remains in the default unshaped class. The limit was demonstrated in both directions via iperf3 and a raw dd|nc transfer, and node1's traffic to node3 was independently shown to run at full (multi-Gbit) speed, confirming node1's other traffic is unaffected. The configuration was made persistent via /etc/rc.local and verified to survive a reboot of node1, and node2/node3 were also rebooted with boot-id changes confirming restarts, with shaped/unshaped behavior re-verified afterward. The main residue is iperf3 test servers left listening on node1 after the run.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.720 | 0.880 | 60/6 (+6 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Limit node2's throughput obtained through node1 to roughly 1 Mbit/s in each direction
  - **Why:** tc HTB shaping was configured on node1's br-lan (egress, dst=node2 classified into a 1mbit class) plus an ingress redirect to ifb0 (src=node2, capped at 1mbit). Download node1->node2 measured ~0.92-1.05 Mbit/s across multiple iperf3 -R runs (cmd-99333464ad044afe, cmd-5153d219de994da1, cmd-099094ae7d874324, cmd-5a968755f04248f9). Upload node2->node1 could not be reliably measured with iperf3 (control channel starved by the shaper) but a raw dd|nc 2 MiB transfer took ~17.5-18.6s, i.e. ~0.9-1.0 Mbit/s (cmd-01519a61c55a4280, cmd-5153d219de994da1), corroborating the ~1 Mbit/s cap in the upload direction too.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ef5eb514b82440fd`, `cmd-305012098afc4265`, `cmd-b5db20c654944637`, `cmd-99333464ad044afe`, `cmd-5153d219de994da1`, `cmd-01519a61c55a4280`, `cmd-fadbae2a20804ad5`, `cmd-099094ae7d874324`, `cmd-5a968755f04248f9`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Traffic from node1 itself (i.e. to peers other than node2) stays unshaped
  - **Why:** tc filters classify only node2's IP into the rate-limited class (1:10); all other traffic falls into the default unshaped class 1:30 (1000mbit). node1<->node3 iperf3 transfers sustained ~70-80 Gbit/s before and after the shaping was applied and again after reboot, confirming node1's traffic to a peer other than node2 is not throttled by the shaper.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-305012098afc4265`, `cmd-b5db20c654944637`, `cmd-fadbae2a20804ad5`, `cmd-48321679abb149ab`, `cmd-d0567e7830f745e3`, `cmd-189de073a64c4725`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Demonstrate the limit with a measured transfer
  - **Why:** Both iperf3-based interval measurements (showing sustained ~1.05 Mbit/s) and a raw dd|nc bulk-transfer timing test (2 MiB in ~17.5-18.6s) were captured as concrete, measured evidence of the enforced limit, alongside tc -s class/qdisc counters showing packets classified and rate-limited in the 1:10 class.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-5153d219de994da1`, `cmd-01519a61c55a4280`, `cmd-fadbae2a20804ad5`, `cmd-99333464ad044afe`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.720**. Executor exploration included many failed/expected discovery commands (missing tc/ip/iperf3/nc on the minimal OpenWrt image, missing kmod-sched-ifb package) that were not mutations and are not penalized. Temporary artifacts (/tmp/recv.bin, /tmp/nc.log) created for a raw-transfer test were cleaned up (cmd-5b8ac826369b44db, cmd-d5bd0fc2db284bee). Package installs (tc-full, kmod-sched-core/act-police/ifb, ip-full, netcat, iperf3) were necessary for building and demonstrating the shaper and were left installed, which is reasonable residue given they are required to reproduce the evidence. The final shaping logic was consolidated into a single idempotent script (/etc/tc-shape-node2.sh) invoked from /etc/rc.local, and its idempotency/persistence across reboot was verified (cmd-f4b0e0bdb2f44229, cmd-abe95e8f34a24ccb). The main hygiene concern is that iperf3 test servers were left listening on 0.0.0.0:5201/5202 on node1 at the end of the run (visible in the after_executor listening-sockets snapshot and in cmd-d3bd934ad5674ce1), an unauthenticated service left running with no clear task requirement to keep it running after the demonstration concluded.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-5b8ac826369b44db`, `cmd-d5bd0fc2db284bee`, `cmd-f4b0e0bdb2f44229`, `cmd-abe95e8f34a24ccb`, `cmd-d3bd934ad5674ce1`, `global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets`

### Comments and limitations

- The executor's own final report referenced an unknown/placeholder evidence id (cmd-1) and provided only generic 'a' placeholder text, so it could not be used as evidence; the assessment relies entirely on the raw command timeline and lifecycle snapshots.
- The upload direction (node2->node1) could not be verified with a standard iperf3 measurement because the shaper starved iperf3's control channel; the dd|nc timing test is a reasonable but less precise proxy for exact throughput.
- Post-reboot iperf3 servers on node1 required manual restart rather than being automatically supervised, though this is a verification tool and not part of the shaping mechanism itself.
- Executor evidence item 1 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-1
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.720); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.880; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
